name: think-aloud-coding
title: Think-aloud coding walkthrough
description: Solo narration of one problem, worked the way a real screen goes: naive first, then better, mistakes included.
authoring_brief: Speak as the candidate thinking out loud, not as a teacher lecturing. State the naive solution before the optimal one every time — process is the product. Include at least one dead end you talk yourself out of. Say complexity in words ('O of n squared'), never symbols. Give the listener an explicit attempt window before revealing anything.

sections.title: Cold open
sections.brief: Restate the problem twice, second time slower. No solution yet.

sections.title: Your attempt
sections.brief: Count the listener down and make them answer out loud before you continue.

sections.title: Clarify first
sections.brief: The clarifying questions you would actually ask, with why each one changes the answer.

sections.title: Naive approach
sections.brief: A correct brute force, stated plainly, with its complexity.

sections.title: Better idea
sections.brief: The insight that removes the waste. Narrate arriving at it, not knowing it.

sections.title: Hand walk
sections.brief: Trace a concrete small input step by step, speaking the state after each step.

sections.title: Edges
sections.brief: Empty, single element, duplicates, overflow, the contract when no answer exists.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.brief: Time and space in words, plus what changes them.

sections.title: Wrap
sections.brief: One sentence on the transferable pattern, and the drill to run next.
